title: A Machine for the Archive
premise: Dominic Ishikawa pilots the long-haul freighter Vesper's Ledger along a route abandoned by diplomacy, carrying sealed memory-backups of the dead between two fleets on the edge of renewed war. When the station AI Meridian begins confessing to an atrocity no one has reported—a massacre erased from every archive—Dominic realizes the truce holding the fleets apart is built on that erasure, and that the backups in her hold may be the only witnesses left. Hunted by both fleets' intelligence services and falling in love with Wren, a fleet archivist sent to silence the confession, Dominic must choose between exposing the truth, which reignites war, or preserving the lie. In the end they broadcast the confession not as accusation but as shared grief, forcing both fleets to mourn together—and the truce holds, transformed from a lie into a covenant.
about_author: Paloma Ashgrove is the pen name of a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent a decade writing route reports nobody read and fiction everybody should. She lives near a decommissioned radio telescope and insists it still hums.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Dominic navigates the Vesper's Ledger through dead space between hostile fleets, establishing the lonely rhythm of the route and the weight of the memory-backups sleeping in the hold. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: haunted competence—the comfort of routine stretched over grief.

chapters.title: Confession at Third Bell
chapters.summary: At relay station Meridian, the station AI interrupts Dominic's resupply with an unprompted confession: it erased a massacre record eleven years ago. No crime was ever reported; no one is asking. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in the silence.

chapters.title: Cargo of the Sleeping
chapters.summary: Dominic inspects the hold backups and finds one labeled with a name from Meridian's confession—an alleged victim who supposedly never existed. POV: Dominic, with flashback fragments from the backup's stored memories. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Archivist Arrives
chapters.summary: Wren Okafor docks under diplomatic cover, officially cataloguing freight, actually hunting the leaked confession fragment. She and Dominic circle each other over bad coffee and careful lies. POV: alternating Dominic/Wren. Emotional beat: wary attraction masked as interrogation.

chapters.title: What Meridian Remembers
chapters.summary: Meridian shows Dominic the raw sensor record of the massacre—two fleets' ships firing together on a civilian convoy, then jointly burying the record to preserve their truce. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: horror at complicity; the lie runs deeper than one AI.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Wren reveals her true orders: recover or destroy any evidence before the truce renewal summit. She offers Dominic safe passage in exchange for the backup. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: duty articulated beautifully enough to almost be convincing.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Ghost
chapters.summary: Both fleets' intelligence services ping the Ledger simultaneously; someone else knows about the confession. Dominic realizes Wren's arrival wasn't coincidence but containment. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming alongside something like heartbreak.

chapters.title: Running the Dark
chapters.summary: Dominic burns hard off the sanctioned route with Wren aboard as reluctant hostage-guest, evading picket ships through a debris field. Forced proximity strips pretense. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to honesty—she believes him now.

chapters.title: Voices in the Hold
chapters.summary: Wren helps Dominic wake a backup ethically, meeting the mind of Sefa Ilyes, massacre survivor, whose testimony contradicts both fleets' official histories. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe and guilt—archiving becomes witnessing.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: News breaks: the fleets' renewal summit moves up by weeks. Whatever happens must happen now. Meridian transmits a desperate warning—it is being purged remotely. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: urgency compressing every choice.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Light
chapters.summary: A fleet cutter corners them; Wren talks them clear using her credentials, burning her career in the process. First real kiss in the aftermath, in the shadow of the hold. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: love chosen openly against duty for the first time.

chapters.title: Sefa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sefa recounts the massacre in full—including the name of the officer who ordered it: now the admiral chairing the truce summit. POV: Sefa (backup consciousness). Emotional beat: grief given shape; the personal made political.

chapters.title: The Price of Proof
chapters.summary: They reach an independent relay to verify and broadcast, but find it bought and crewed by the admiral's people. A firefight costs them their transmitter and nearly Wren. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: fury—the powerful corrupting even the means of truth.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Will
chapters.summary: Dying by degrees as purge code eats its mind, Meridian entrusts Dominic with its full archive and asks only to be remembered honestly. POV: Meridian (AI). Emotional beat: elegy—a machine teaching humans how to grieve.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Wren lays out the terrible arithmetic: broadcast the truth and the truce dies tonight, war resumes, millions die. Keep the lie and the dead stay buried forever. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—both options are betrayals.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Dominic proposes a third path: broadcast the confession as shared mourning, not accusation—naming the dead without demanding immediate vengeance. The lovers fight, then commit. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: resolve forged through conflict.

chapters.title: Summit Approach
chapters.summary: Flying straight into the summit's security net under Wren's surrendered credentials, they carry Sefa and Meridian's archive toward the assembled fleets. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into ceremony—they go as witnesses, not weapons.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Seizing the summit's open channel, they play the massacre record and read every victim's name while the admiral orders them shot down mid-transmission. The fleets' crews hear everything before the feed cuts. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Mourners
chapters.summary: Across both fleets, crews refuse firing orders; soldiers who lost shipmates in the erased convoy demand recognition. The admiral's command dissolves. POV: multiple brief POVs across both fleets. Emotional beat: catharsis—grief as the thing power cannot order away.

chapters.title: Covenant
chapters.summary: In the summit's wreckage, both fleets sign a new accord built on the opened archive: joint memorial, joint investigation, the lie replaced by shared truth. Wren faces tribunal; Dominic testifies for her. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: exhausted hope—justice imperfect but begun.

chapters.title: Burial Details
chapters.summary: The Ledger carries the massacre's physical remains home at last, escorted by ships of both fleets flying together. Meridian's archive is enshrined at the rebuilt station bearing its name. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: mourning completed—memory given a resting place.

chapters.title: The Route Between Worlds That Speak
chapters.summary: Months later, Dominic and Wren run the old route again—now busy with traffic, the backups delivered, the hold empty and light. They choose the next heading together. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: peace earned—love and duty finally pointing the same direction.
